alignment_findings.detail: All 20 modules have Hebrew and English counterparts with the same publication URN or div @corresp. The source keys in units.json map one-to-one onto the files.

shetargilenu-/gomel_chasadim (both languages): the shetargilenu prayer-part milestone opens the paragraph, and the gomel_chasadim milestone sits right after לְהִשְׁתַּעְבֶּד־לָךְ in Hebrew and after 'force our inclination to serve Thee;' in English, so both scopes cover matching extents. The bare prayer-part terminator closes gomel_chasadim in both. The pb n=7 sits before לְהִשְׁתַּעְבֶּד in Hebrew and before 'the good inclination' in English, which matches the printed breaks. The div has no @corresp, so the file does not falsely claim to be the whole shetargilenu.
The duplicated English sheasani_kirtzono line is kept inside the same div URN as a choice with sic and an empty corr. The Hebrew has one paragraph. Alignment is at div level, so there is no drift.

The לעולם directive sits at the same position in both documentary morning_blessings files, with facs n49 for Hebrew and n50 for English. The women's conditional note is xml:lang="en" in both languages, which matches the English italics printed on the Hebrew page.
The facs and pb page images are consistent: s48→n47, s49→n48, s50→n49, s51→n50. biblScope is 6–6 for the p.6 modules, 6–7 for shetargilenu, and 7–7 for the rest.

order_findings.detail: Both documentary morning_blessings files follow the printed order: Elohai Neshamah → lasekhvi, shelo_asani_goy, shelo_asani_aved, [men gate] shelo_asani_ishah, [women gate plus source note] sheasani_kirtzono, poqeach … hamaavir_shenah, shetargilenu-/gomel_chasadim, shetatzileni, לעולם directive, ribbon_kol_haolamim, aval_anachnu.

Expanded: section_morning_hashachar_continuation comes after section_morning_opening_blessings, which holds the German Neshamah, the other-rite Torah block and the other-rite Neshamah, and before section_morning_torah_german_later. The German order is Asher Yatzar → Neshamah → hashachar … Aval Anachnu → Torah blessings, Num 6:24–26, Ellu Devarim. Other rites have the full Torah block between Asher Yatzar and Neshamah. Nothing is placed after Aval Anachnu beyond the existing later block, and the gender gates are independent of the rite and Shabbat conditions.

Expanded gender alternatives use opensiddur:person/gender with symbol male/female. The condition-own bilingual labels (לאנשים/Men say:, לנשים/Women say:) print only when gender is undefined. The shared word modules are transcluded without gates. The range transclusion uses target shetargilenu and targetEnd gomel_chasadim. The new continuation needs no navigation refs.
